findings.title: User storage is given raw codes, not a recovery-code credential
findings.body: createRecoveryCodesCredential hands every supporting user-storage provider a UserCredentialModel whose value is a JSON array of plaintext recovery codes, and then skips RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.createCredential entirely when updateCredential returns true. Local credentials store a RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel (hashed codes, next-code index, generated-at, label) and consume a code inside isValid. Federated providers never receive that model, so they cannot persist the same structure. A provider that stores the challenge response and later returns it from getCredentials will cause RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel to fail when the login form or authenticator loads the credential. Code consumption, exhaustion, and reconfigure-when-empty also never run in Keycloak for this path, because those side effects live only in the local provider that was skipped.

findings.title: Last federated recovery code is not removed
findings.body: After a successful recovery-code login the authenticator now loads the credential via RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential, which prefers a federated credential. If that model reports allCodesUsed, it still calls credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById. That API only deletes a credential in Keycloak's local store. A federated id is not found, so the exhausted credential stays in user storage, isConfiguredFor remains true, and the user can be stuck with a recovery-code authenticator that no longer has a usable code. The required action added just below does not disable the federated credential either.

findings.title: Login form crashes when federated credential cannot be parsed
findings.body: The bean calls RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) and immediately uses credentialModelOpt.get() and getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get() with no empty check. configuredFor only checks isConfiguredFor, which a user-storage provider can answer without exposing a RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel. If the federated stream is empty, or the stored credentialData is the raw JSON list written by CredentialHelper rather than recovery-code credential data, rendering the recovery-code login page throws NoSuchElementException or a deserialization error instead of a challenge.

findings.title: Test storage accepts any recovery code and never consumes it
findings.body: isValid deserializes the stored JSON list and returns true if any code equals the submitted value. It does not require the next unused code, does not remove the used code, and does not record a counter. The same code can be replayed indefinitely, and allCodesUsed() can never become true because getCredentials rebuilds a fresh model from the original list via createFromValues. The new login test only submits code 0 once, so it does not catch this. The provider is the reference for the new user-storage contract, so it encodes a weaker, reusable-secret check instead of recovery-code semantics.

findings.title: getCredentials NPEs and drops the stored credential id
findings.body: getCredentials calls getMyUser(user) and immediately dereferences myUser.recoveryCodes. getMyUser returns null when the username is missing, so the stream throws NullPointerException; isConfiguredFor already guards that case. When a credential exists, the method ignores the id assigned in updateCredential and calls RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues, which hashes the raw codes again and allocates a new id on every read. Account-console or authenticator deletes by that id cannot match the stored credential, and used-code state cannot be represented.

findings.title: Recovery codes cannot be disabled in the test storage
findings.body: disableCredentialType clears only OTP. Recovery codes are now supportsCredentialType/isConfiguredFor/updateCredential, but disabling them logs 'Unsupported' and leaves myUser.recoveryCodes set. Admin REST and account-console removal use disableCredentialType for federated credentials, so a recovery-code credential created by this provider cannot be removed the way OTP can. getDisableableCredentialTypesStream also never advertises the recovery-code type.

findings.title: Recovery-codes feature is enabled without a server restart
findings.body: The new test is annotated @EnableFeature(value = RECOVERY_CODES, skipRestart = true). RecoveryAuthnCodesAction is an EnvironmentDependentProviderFactory whose isSupported check runs when the server starts. With skipRestart, the required-action and authenticator factories are not reloaded, so CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES and the recovery-code browser flow can be missing or inert. The test then either fails or never exercises federated recovery-code setup.
